subject: Private instance boundary review & evidence request for GreenBank SOC/SIG
messages:
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@greenbank.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify scope for penetration test evidence on GreenBank private instance

Hi Alex / Laura,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our compliance team has been reviewing the SIG intake and the SOC 2 checklist, and the external auditors have asked for a few environment-specific artifacts related to our private instance deployment (GreenBank tenant). Before we hand things off to them, can you confirm the exact boundary definition Redwood used for the Dec 2025 penetration test for our environment? Specifically we need:

- The network boundary: which subnets and IP ranges were in scope (public vs private), and whether the test exercised the transit gateway/VPN endpoints or only the internal tenant subnets.
- Access vectors tested: did the assessment include the customer-managed bastion/SSH jump host and the transit gateway rules?
- Authentication / secrets: confirmation that KMS keys used by the runtime are customer-managed or Redwood-managed for this tenant (we believe customer-managed KMS is in place but need the authoritative config).
- Evidence: redacted penetration test report (high-level findings), host-level agent confirmations, flow logs (sample), and the boundary diagram you referenced.

We want to be sure we only upload artifacts that align with our internal data-classification rules (PII redaction, no private keys attached). Can you send a short note describing the scope used, and attach whatever redacted evidence you can provide? If some items require a POA&M or are still in remediation, please call those out with ticket numbers and ETA.

Carla from AuditCo will be in the loop for the redaction/acceptability — copying her here.

Thanks,
Amir

Amir Patel
Security Compliance Lead, GreenBank Financial
amir.patel@greenbank.com

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@greenbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-12T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify scope for penetration test evidence on GreenBank private instance

Amir — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: the Dec 2025 external assessment covered the customer tenant subnets and the Redwood runtime instances that are anchored in GreenBank's VPC; transit/VPN edges were in scope for unauthenticated network checks but we did not perform credentialed testing against your managed bastion. Attached is the boundary diagram (private_instance_boundary_diagram_v2.png) and a scope inventory CSV that maps hosts/subnets to the findings we can share.

Key details: 
- Network boundary: in-scope were the tenant private subnets (10.44.32.0/20), the NAT gateway addresses used by the runtime egress, and the Redwood-facing peering endpoint (10.200.8.0/28). The transit gateway attachments were observed; the assessor performed unauthenticated reachability checks against the TGW-managed endpoints only (no credentialed TGW config testing).
- Access vectors: credentialed host-level testing was limited to Redwood-managed runtime instances (we used agent-based collection on those instances). We did not SSH to your customer-managed bastion. Where customer-managed components were relevant (bastion, in-VPC K8s control plane), we verified publicly-exposed ports and validated authentication requirements but did not attempt credentialed privilege escalation.
- KMS: GreenBank is configured to use customer-managed CMKs in your AWS account for data-at-rest used by the tenant; we have included the KMS key ARN references in the inventory CSV. The pen-test did not and could not access raw key material.

Attachments included: private_instance_boundary_diagram_v2.png, scope_inventory_greenbank.csv.

We also have a redacted summary from the third-party assessor; they prefer to send the report directly to GreenBank's security contacts (Carla / Amir) as it contains internal hostnames. I'll ask them to publish a redacted PDF to the link below.

For remediation status, looping in Rishi (remediation owner) and Laura (CS lead) — see inline expectations.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai

From: PenTest Ltd <reports@pentest-ltd.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, Amir Patel <amir.patel@greenbank.com>
Cc: Carla Vargas <carla.vargas@auditco.io>
Date: 2026-01-14T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Redacted external assessment summary for GreenBank (Dec 2025)

Hi all,

Attached is the redacted executive summary from the December 2025 external assessment we performed for Redwood's GreenBank tenant. Attachment: redacted_pentest_summary_2025-12.pdf (contains executive findings and high-level repro steps only; hostnames and exact IPs removed per agreement).

High-level: 3 medium findings, 4 low findings. None of the medium findings provided evidence of lateral movement into GreenBank-managed systems. We flagged one configuration issue related to a container runtime that allowed excessive capabilities on a helper container (PN-2025-047), which Redwood remediated in patch v2025.12.3 (see our remediation note).

We can provide a scoped CSV of findings mapped to inventory IDs (redacted) if GreenBank's team wants to ingest it into their tracker. We will not include private keys or PII in any artifacts.

Regards,
PenTest Ltd — Reports Team
reports@pentest-ltd.com

Subject: Re: Clarify scope for penetration test evidence on GreenBank private instance

Amir — following up with the artifacts and remediation status. Per Alex's note above and the pen test summary from PenTest Ltd, we've uploaded the allowed artifacts to the GreenBank evidence bucket and the tenant dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/tenants/greenbank-123/evidence

What we've provided: 
- redacted_pentest_summary_2025-12.pdf (executive summary from assessor) — uploaded and accessible to your security group.
- private_instance_boundary_diagram_v2.png — shows the in-scope subnets and conditioned egress paths.
- scope_inventory_greenbank.csv — maps inventory IDs to redacted host tags and KMS ARNs.
- Sample VPC Flow Logs (sample window: 2025-11-15T00:00Z to 2025-11-15T06:00Z) — included in the evidence package as flow_samples.csv (redacted to remove IPs outside scope).

Remediation status (short):
- PN-2025-047 (container capability issue) — resolved in v2025.12.3; remediation ticket REM-2391 (closed).
- Medium finding #2 (temporary S3 ACL exposure) — mitigation applied (bucket policy tightened), follow-up validation scheduled (Jira: SEC-1294). ETA for final validation: 2026-01-24.
- Low findings — addressed or accepted; detail in scope_inventory_greenbank.csv.

Next actions for GreenBank: please confirm Carla/AuditCo accept the redacted summary and let us know if you need additional evidence (e.g., full flow logs with IPs under NDA, or signed SOC attestation excerpts). If you want the full pen-test report shared directly from PenTest Ltd under an NDA, we can coordinate that flow.
